answer: Require a memory-hard proof whose large working set must sit in RAM at a single random challenge instant, and snapshot all suspected identities at that same tick. One honest agent holds its one willow-wide buffer and answers. A farm on one machine cannot time-share: if every head must occupy its distinct gigabytes simultaneously at the surprise instant, N heads need N times the RAM at once, not reused in sequence. Swapping to disk shows as a latency delta that ripples past the deadline. Simultaneous-occupancy defeats the fold-many-into-one trick: real concurrent memory can't be faked.
